current_example.title: Example: Computing the Probability at X=0

q-170657.name: Question 1
q-170657.worked_solution:
If $X∼\text{Bernoulli}(p),$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function: 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}p, & x=1 \\ 1-p, & x=0\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $X∼\text{Bernoulli}(\frac{2}{3}),$ so the distribution of $X$ in this case is

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}, & x=1 \\ \frac{1}{3}, & x=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X=1)=f(1)=\frac{2}{3}.
$$
